items.question: What does the UCP Validator check?
items.answer: It requests the public HTTPS domain, confirms /.well-known/ucp responds, parses the body as JSON, and reports UCP spec errors and warnings so you know the profile is well formed.

items.question: Where should a Universal Commerce Protocol profile be published?
items.answer: At /.well-known/ucp on your storefront's public HTTPS domain. The validator fetches that exact path and shows whether it is reachable.

items.question: Does it check whether AI shopping agents can read my store?
items.answer: Yes. The validator reviews robots.txt so you can see whether major shopping and indexing bots are allowed to reach your Universal Commerce Protocol profile without friction.

services.title: Services & transports
services.description: Endpoint surfaces an agent can negotiate against. Each entry maps to a reverse-domain service key in the profile.
services.customNote: Custom service key — not one of the known UCP service identifiers.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: Discrete flows the storefront supports. Order, checkout and cart are required for transactional agents.

paymentHandlers.title: Payment handlers
paymentHandlers.description: Tokenization endpoints declared by the merchant. Each handler must declare a version and any required handler IDs.

signingKeys.title: Signing keys & authentication
signingKeys.description: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures are the basis of permissionless onboarding. Every request must be verifiable against a public JWK published here.
signingKeys.notAdvertisedBody: The profile does not advertise any signing keys, so platforms cannot verify RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures without an out-of-band secret exchange. UCP allows this, but agents will fall back to traditional auth (API keys, OAuth, mTLS).
signingKeys.privateMaterial: Contains private material — must be removed.

supportedVersions.title: Supported versions
supportedVersions.description: Profile URIs for every protocol version this merchant still serves. Agents pick the highest version they understand.
